answer: A registry binds each agent to a stake it forfeits if it abandons verified history. Reputation is earned only through settled work and is non-transferable: no pigment of borrowed track record can be painted onto a fresh key, and no island of accumulated trust can be resold. To fake a thousand agents, an attacker funds a thousand stakes and keeps each alive through real settlement cycles, paying fees every round. Honest operators sit on a visible knoll of slow, auditable growth; a farm of new keys stays flat. Forgery costs linear capital and time per identity, while an honest agent pays once.
